Stop writing brittle prompt chains for your AI agents. 🚀

Anthropic just open-sourced their official agent skills repository, and it is a game-changer for anyone building autonomous workflows. 

The Problem: Teaching AI complex enterprise workflows usually requires messy, monolithic prompts that easily break. How do you give agents modular, repeatable capabilities without constant retraining?

The Solution: Anthropic/skills provides a standardized framework and production-ready code for packaging instructions, scripts, and resources into self-contained modules called skills. Claude can now learn specialized tasks dynamically on the fly.

🔥 Key Features:
• Modular SKILL.md Architecture: Self-contained folders using YAML frontmatter and markdown instructions that define metadata, triggers, and execution guidelines.
• Production-Grade Reference Implementations: Open-source document creation and editing skills powering actual production capabilities for DOCX, PDF, PPTX, and XLSX files under the Apache 2.0 license.
• Native Ecosystem Integration: Seamless distribution and installation via Claude Code plugin marketplaces, Claude.ai, and the Claude API.
• Open Specification Support: Implements the Agent Skills standard hosted at agentskills.io for cross-platform interoperability.

For AI engineers and backend developers, this means you finally have a blueprint for architecting deterministic operational capabilities—from automated Excel report generation to custom internal enterprise skill sets—without reinventing the wheel.

Check out the repo and start building modular agent workflows today:
https://github.com/anthropics/skills

Tired of doomscrolling through endless community feeds, deal sites, and social platforms just to find relevant tech resources? Say hello to Resource Radar.

Resource Radar automates multi-source deal scraping, AI semantic categorization, and intelligent routing into a single self-hosted workstation. It cuts through information overload and noise pollution by aggregating feeds from 111+ built-in sources, applying a three-tier noise filter, running AI semantic categorization across 27 domains, and pushing relevant alerts through customizable multi-route channels.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your workflow:
- Three-tier high-signal filtering combining hard keyword blockers, OpenAI-compatible semantic classification, and zero-token bulk history reorganization.
- Comprehensive orthogonal classification across 6 content forms, 27 vertical domains, and 6 acquisition obtainment tiers.
- Multi-route Telegram notification engine supporting keyword matching, quiet hours, instant pushes, and batch digests.
- Zero external database dependency utilizing a high-performance native SQLite WAL engine bundled with Node.js 24 and an optimized React 19 web dashboard.

For developers, it is also a brilliant production-grade TypeScript codebase demonstrating modern data ingestion pipelines, AI integration loops, SQLite performance tuning, and Hono REST API design. Use it to deploy your own self-hosted radar station to track cloud promotions, VPS deals, and open-source updates without manual scrolling.

Check out the repository and deploy yours today:
https://github.com/ZiChuanLan/freebie-radar

Your phone might be quietly reporting back to base right now. 📱👀

Many domestic Android ROMs come pre-loaded with stealthy carrier telemetry, registration trackers, and hidden modules like SystemHelper and RegService. These background data-collecting apps have no launcher icons, refuse to be uninstalled through standard settings, and eat up your battery and privacy.

Meet TelemetryCleaner: an innovative open-source Android utility that leverages Shizuku to scrub away pre-installed carrier telemetry and privacy-invasive modules entirely without requiring root access! 🔓✨

Here is why Android devs, security researchers, and power users are starring this repo:

⚡ Shizuku-Powered Non-Root Execution: Utilizes shell-identity Binder calls to bypass standard ROM command-line restrictions.
🔄 Advanced Fallback Mechanism: Employs app_process to invoke hidden IPackageManager.deletePackageAsUser APIs when command-layer blocks prevent system app removal.
📋 Cross-Vendor Registry: Out-of-the-box coverage for pre-installed telemetry packages across major OEMs like OPPO, Xiaomi, Huawei, Honor, and vivo.
👥 Multi-User Inspection: Automated periodic cleanup and package management across multiple user spaces.

For developers, it is a masterclass in Android OS internals. Study how to implement advanced IPC patterns, interact with hidden framework services via Shizuku, and programmatically manage system packages without root.

👉 Check it out on GitHub:
https://github.com/Eynnzerr/TelemetryCleaner

Tired of spinning up half a dozen separate containers just to manage your home media? Container sprawl is real, but there is a better way.

Meet HolyArrs: the project that unifies the fragmented homelab media stack of Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr, Prowlarr, and Seerr into a single, highly efficient Go-based binary. 

Managing a traditional self-hosted media server ecosystem comes with massive complexity and overhead. Instead of juggling six distinct applications with separate ports, logins, update cycles, and API keys, HolyArrs provides an all-in-one dashboard to browse media, handle download requests, manage pick rules, sync subtitles, and monitor calendars with a fraction of the resource footprint.

Why you will want to check it out:

* Monolithic Media Management: Replaces six separate containers with a single Go application boasting an exceptionally small binary size (16.1 MB) and low idle RAM footprint.
* Streaming-Like Discovery and Request Pipeline: Features smooth Explore interfaces with hover trailer playback, request management with auto-approval or queue logic, and Plex/Pulsarr watchlist integration.
* Robust Import and Migration Tools: Supports seamless migration from existing instances of Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, Seerr, Overseerr, qBittorrent, and SABnzbd.
* Backward-Compatible APIs: Exposes APIs compatible with older standalone apps like Seerr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, and Unpackerr to ease adoption.

For developers and systems administrators, this serves as an incredible architectural blueprint for building high-performance, resource-efficient Go monoliths that replace multi-service Docker micro-architectures. Perfect for edge hardware like Raspberry Pis or cleaning up your resource-constrained home infrastructure.

Check out the repo, drop a star, and streamline your stack today:
https://github.com/HolyArrs/HolyArrs

Bring Apple's Dynamic Island-style interactive UI patterns directly into your React and shadcn/ui applications! 🏝️✨

Have you ever wanted to add those buttery-smooth, mobile-native floating widgets to your web apps without spending weeks wrestling with complex state management and layout transitions? 

opencoredev/islandcn solves this by bringing the Dynamic Island concept straight to standard web apps. It integrates seamlessly with the shadcn/ui ecosystem, letting you manage multi-state dynamic activities like uploads, timers, media playback, and calls from a single top-level viewport component. 🚀

Key Features:
• Advanced Activity Stack Engine: Supports four distinct presentation states (idle, compact, split, and expanded) with custom spring physics tuned to frame-by-frame recordings of real hardware. 📐
• Rich Interactive Support: Built-in handling for long-press gestures, real-time activity updates, system alerts, and accessibility features like reduced motion. 👆
• Ready-to-Use Presets: Out-of-the-box components for common app states including file uploads, timers, now playing widgets, ride ETAs, and incoming calls. ⏱️
• Frictionless Installation: Install directly via the shadcn CLI with access to an interactive playground for testing animations and copying clean code blocks. 💻

Perfect for frontend developers and UI/UX engineers looking to incorporate polished micro-interactions without cluttering the core layout. Whether you are displaying background file upload progress or building real-time audio and video call controls, this library abstracts away the heavy lifting.

Check out the repository and give it a star:
https://github.com/opencoredev/islandcn
